claims.text: Increasing or decreasing the percentage of a single element in HfNbTaTiZr will produce systematic variations in local mechanical properties such as hardness.
Changes in elemental concentration affect solid-solution strengthening in HfNbTaTiZr.
The baseline HfNbTaTiZr alloy is equiatomic or near-equiatomic and has previously reported mechanical properties.
Multi-target DC magnetron sputtering can create compositional-gradient HfNbTaTiZr thin films by varying individual target deposition rates.
The proposed films are deposited at approximately 25°C for 30–60 minutes.
Varying elemental percentages causes local variations in the alloy microstructure.
Varying elemental percentages changes local solid-solution-strengthening levels.
Compositional gradients may cause compositional clusters to form.
Changing individual elemental percentages changes lattice distortion.
Changing individual elemental percentages changes defect structures.
Changes in lattice distortion and defect structures modulate resistance to plastic deformation.
Enrichment in an element that promotes solid-solution strengthening is expected to enhance hardness and yield strength.
Depletion of an element that weakens the matrix is expected to enhance hardness and yield strength.
The compositional-gradient film will provide a continuous spatial map of mechanical properties.
Regions richer in the element contributing most strongly to solid-solution strengthening will have greater hardness than the near-equiatomic baseline.
The near-equiatomic, non-gradient baseline has uniform mechanical properties when deposited under identical conditions.
The expected trends apply primarily to room-temperature sputtered thin films.
The thin-film trends may not extrapolate to bulk or higher-temperature-processed materials because diffusion effects become significant.
The quantitative mechanical-property contribution of each constituent element is uncertain.
Synergistic interactions among elements may complicate correlations between individual elemental changes and mechanical properties.
